cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has already watched Pharaoh, king of Egypt, promise to let God's people go and then go back on it (Exodus 8:8, 15). Now the LORD tells Moses to get up early and meet Pharaoh when he goes out to the water. No snooze button, friend, NONE.
The LORD's message for Pharaoh: "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me." And if Pharaoh still won't, something is headed his way.

cards.question: If Pharaoh won't let the people go, what does the LORD say He'll send?

cards.text: The LORD says the flies will be on Pharaoh, his officials, his people and their houses, even the ground where they stand. But on that day, the land of Goshen will get special treatment.

cards.question: The LORD says the land of Goshen will have no swarms of flies at all. Who lives there?
Why does the LORD say He'll keep the flies out of the place where His people live?

answers.text: So Pharaoh will know the LORD is in the land
So the Israelites can hide there from Pharaoh
So Moses will have a safe place to pray

cards.text: The sign is set for tomorrow, and the LORD does it: thick swarms of flies pour into Pharaoh's palace and his officials' houses, and all through Egypt the land is ruined. I once spent an HOUR swinging my mustache at ONE fly in my bakery, so I can't even imagine.

Pharaoh calls in Moses and Aaron, Moses' brother, and says, "Go, sacrifice to your God within this land." Friend, that's like your boss saying you can take the day off, as long as you stay at your desk.

cards.question: Moses takes Pharaoh's offer to sacrifice to God right there in Egypt.

cards.text: Moses says it would not be right, because their sacrifices to the LORD would be detestable to the Egyptians. Then he asks, "…will they not stone us?"

cards.question: Moses won't offer these sacrifices where the Egyptians can see. Where does he say they must go to sacrifice?

answers.text: Over to the land of Goshen
Down to the banks of the Nile

cards.question: Pharaoh says he'll let them go sacrifice in the wilderness, but they must not go very ___.

cards.text: Then Pharaoh adds, "Now pray for me." Negotiating the deal and asking for a favor in the SAME breath, friend, that takes nerve.

cards.question: When Pharaoh asks for prayer, Moses warns him not to act deceitfully again.
Moses prays, and the LORD does as Moses asked. How many flies are left on Pharaoh and his people?

answers.text: Only the ones in the palace

cards.question: Once the flies are gone, Pharaoh keeps his word and lets the people go.

cards.text: Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well. That's two promises and two take-backs, friend, and I'm starting to notice a pattern.
Then the LORD sends Moses back to Pharaoh with that line again: "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me." Moses has walked this road so many times, friend, he could do it with his eyes closed.
If Pharaoh keeps refusing, the hand of the LORD will bring a severe plague on his livestock in the field. Horses, donkeys, camels, herds and flocks.

cards.question: The LORD says a few of Israel's animals will still die, just fewer than Egypt's.
The flies came on the day the LORD set. This time, the LORD says He'll bring the plague on Egypt's livestock ___.

cards.text: The next day, the LORD does just that. All the livestock of the Egyptians die, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites dies.

cards.question: Pharaoh sends officials and learns that not one of Israel's animals died. What does Pharaoh do?

answers.text: He still refuses to let the people go
He lets the people go at last
He has his magicians copy it

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses and Aaron to grab handfuls of soot from the furnace. Friend, I KNOW soot, because I've left a batch in the oven too long more times than I can count.

cards.question: Moses is to toss the soot into the air where Pharaoh can see. What does the LORD say it will become over all of Egypt?
Fine dust over all of Egypt. What does the LORD say will break out on man and beast?

cards.text: So they take soot from the furnace and stand before Pharaoh, and Moses tosses it into the air. Festering boils break out on man and beast, and friend, that is NOT the kind of dust you just wipe off the counter.

cards.question: Pharaoh's magicians can't stand before Moses. Why not?

answers.text: Boils broke out on them too
They had run off in fear

cards.question: This time, Pharaoh's heart is hardened by the ___.

cards.text: Pharaoh won't listen, just as the LORD had said to Moses. Flies, livestock, boils, and he STILL won't budge, so trust me, friend, this story is far from over.
